Line of Business: All G.E.H.A Medical Plans
Authorizations are issued for 6 (six) months, unless the ordering physician requests a different timespan or the patients' unique circumstance or condition supports the medical necessity for a different authorization timeframe. Reauthorization requests are reviewed for efficacy, safety and tolerability.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

section: Indication Specific Criteria Breast cancer – unresectable or metastatic
text:
## Indication Specific Criteria Breast cancer – unresectable or metastatic
- The member is 18 years of age or older; AND
- The member has an ECOG performance status of 0-1 1 ; AND
- The member has hormone receptor (HR) positive disease; AND
- The member has HER2 negative (IHC 0, IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-) disease; AND
- Datroway is used as subsequent therapy after the following:
- Endocrine Therapy; AND
- Chemotherapy; AND
- Enhertu (if member is eligible for treatment with Enhertu, as per current version of NCCN Guidelines)
1 0 to 1 - ECOG score of 2 or 3 will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

section: EGFR-Mutated Non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer – locally advanced or metastatic
text:
# EGFR-Mutated Non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer – locally advanced or metastatic
- The member is 18 years of age or older; AND
- The member has an ECOG performance status of 0-1 2 ; AND
- The member has one of the following EGFR mutations: exon 19 deletion, L858R, L861Q, exon 20 insertion, S7681, or G719X; AND
- Has not had prior treatment with:
- Any agent including antibody drug conjugate (ADC) containing a chemotherapeutic agent targeting topoisomerase I; OR
- TROP2-targeted therapy
- Datroway will be used as subsequent therapy after the following:
- Platinum-based (i.e. carboplatin, cisplatin) systemic chemotherapy; AND
- EGFR-directed therapy (i.e. afatinib, dacomitinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, osimertinib)

## Universal Approval Criteria:
Unless otherwise noted, the review criteria used by OncoHealth to determine medical necessity for anticancer treatments and supportive agents include, but is not limited to:
- National Comprehensive Cancer Network® (NCCN) - use consistent with NCCN recommendations carrying a Category 1 or 2A level of evidence; OR
- United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) labeling - new drugs or regimens (combinations of drugs) consistent with the product labeling; OR
- Indications not included in the official FDA labeling or recommended by NCCN (Category 1 or 2A level of evidence) may be considered if determined to be medically necessary per one or more of the following compendia:
- Clinical Pharmacology (Strong For); OR
- Wolters Kluwer Lexi-Drugs® (Level A); OR
- Other uses of drugs and biologics may be considered medically necessary if supported as safe and effective according to peer-reviewed articles from one of the following journals:
- American Journal of Medicine; Annals of Internal Medicine; Annals of Oncology; Annals of Surgical Oncology; Biology of Blood and Marrow Transplantation; Blood; Bone Marrow Transplantation; British Journal of Cancer; British Journal of Hematology; British Medical Journal; Cancer; Clinical Cancer Research; Drugs; European Journal of Cancer (formerly the European Journal of Cancer and Clinical Oncology); Gynecologic Oncology; International Journal of Radiation, Oncology, Biology, and Physics; The Journal of the American Medical Association, Journal of Clinical Oncology; Journal of the National Cancer Institute; Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN); Journal of Urology; Lancet; Lancet Oncology; Leukemia; The New England Journal of Medicine; Radiation Oncology;
- Meeting abstracts and case reports are excluded from consideration;
